sentences: Why are some USB ports blue?
Blue usually marks USB 3, also called SuperSpeed.
The first version of it runs at up to 5 gigabits per second.
The black ports beside it are usually USB 2.
That tops out at 480 megabits per second, roughly 10 times slower.
But the color is a convention, not a rule.
Some makers use red, teal, or plain black for fast ports.
The SS logo next to the port, or your manual, is the better clue.
So plug your fast flash drive or external SSD into the faster port.
